sentences.text: By way of this application which is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as `the Code' for short), the applicant seeks quashing of the criminal complaint bearing no.27464 of 2008 for the offences punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as `the PFA Act' for short) filed by respondent no.1 pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C.,Surat.

2. Learned advocate Mr.Manan Shah for the applicant submitted that he has received instructions to appear on behalf of the applicant and he will file vakalatnama within a period of three days from today.

Heard learned advocate Mr.Manan Shah for the applicant and learned APP Mr.Devnani for the respondent-State.
3.

Learned advocate Mr.Shah for the applicant submits that the impugned complaint came to be filed against the applicant and others under the provisions of the PFA Act alleging the violation of the provisions of the said Act.
It is alleged in the said complaint that the present applicant is working as a Manager of the firm namely Shri Ronak Beverages and Food P.Ltd.

It is alleged that sample of packaged drinking water was taken on 27.3.2008 and after following the HC-NIC Page 2 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT procedure prescribed under the said Act, sample was sent to the local laboratory for necessary analysis.

The concerned Laboratory submitted the report on 5.5.2008 in which the concerned public analyst gave his opinion that the sample of packaged drinking water is adulterated as it does not comply with the microbiological standards laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulterated Rules, 1955 (hereinafter referred to as `PFA Rules' for short) in respect of aerobic microbial counts.

Similarly,
for another sample, similar opinion was given by the concerned public analyst.
It is contended that though the shelf life of the product in question was upto 26.9.2008, the impugned complaint came to be filed on 20.10.2008.
It is, therefore, submitted that the impugned complaint is filed after the shelf life of the drinking water in question has expired.

Thus, it is submitted that the applicant-accused could not request to the trial Court for sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory and therefore he lost the opportunity for sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory.
Hence, prejudice is caused to the applicant-accused.
It is further alleged that the complainant has thereby violated the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the PFA Act.

Learned advocate for the applicant, therefore, requested that the impugned complaint be quashed HC-NIC Page 3 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT and set aside only on this ground.

4. Learned advocate Mr.Shah appearing for the applicant has placed reliance upon the order dated 1.2.2016 passed by this Court in Criminal Revision Application No.475 of 2011 in the case of State of Gujarat V/s Nareshkumar Gordhandas Hotvani in support of his contention.

Learned APP Mr.Devnani has fairly submitted that the decision upon which the reliance is placed by the learned advocate for the applicant is applicable to the facts of the present case.

(2A) When an application is made to the Court under subsection (2), the Court shall require the Local (Health) Authority to forward the part or parts of the sample kept by the said Authority and upon such requisition being made, the said Authority shall forward the part or parts of the sample to the Court within a period of five days from the date of receipt of such requisition.

(2B) On receipt of the part or parts of the sample from the Local (Health) Authority under subsection (2A), the Court shall first ascertain that the mark and seal or fastening as provided in clause (b) of subsection (1) of section 11 are intact and the signature or thumb impression, as the case may be, is not tampered with, and dispatch the part or, as the case may be, one of the parts of the sample under its own seal to the Director of the Central Food Laboratory who shall thereupon send a certificate to the Court in the prescribed form within one month from the date of receipt of the part of the sample specifying the result of the analysis.

sentences.text: Thus, all the aforesaid provisions are pari materia and therefore decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana (supra) as well as in the case of M/s. Medicamen Biotech Limited (supra) are applicable to the facts of the present case.

11. In the case of M/s. Medicamen Biotech Limited (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed in paragraph No.10 as under:
"10.

We find that this judgment helps the case of the appellant rather than that of the respondent because in spite of two communications from the appellant that it intended to adduce evidence to controvert the facts given in the report of the Government Analyst, the fourth sample with the Magistrate had not been sent for reanalysis.
The observations in Amery Pharmaceuticals's case (supra) are also to the same effect.

We find that the aforesaid interpretation supports the case of the appellants inasmuch HC-NIC Page 9 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT they had been deprived of the right to have the fourth sample tested from the Central Drugs Laboratory.

It is also clear that the complaint had been filed on the 2nd July 2002 which is about a month short of the expiry date of the drug and as such had the accused appellant appeared before the Magistrate even on 2nd July 2002 it would have been well nigh impossible to get the sample tested before its expiry.

In the affidavit filed to the petition by Dr. D. Rao,
Deputy Drugs Controller, and in arguments before us, it has been repeatedly stressed that the delay in sending of the sample to the Central Drugs Laboratory had occurred as the appellant had avoided service of summons on it till 9th May 2005.
This is begging the question.

We find that there is no explanation as to why the complaint itself had been filed about a month before the expiry of the shelf life of the drug and concededly the filing of the complaint had nothing to do with the appearance of the accused in response to the notices which were to be issued by the Court after the complaint had been filed.

Likewise, we observe that the requests for retesting of the drug had been made by the appellant in August/September 2001 as would be clear Sunilkumar Vinodbhai Shah vs C S Gohil on 10 August, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62671749/
6 from the facts already given above and there is absolutely no reason as to why the complaint could not have been filed earlier and the fourth sample sent for retesting well within time.

sentences.text:
We are, therefore, of the opinion that the facts of the case suggest that the appellants have been deprived of a valuable right under Section 25(3) and 25(4) of the Act which must necessitate the quashing of the proceedings against them."
14.

Keeping in mind the aforesaid provisions of law and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court and this Court, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present case when the complainant Food Inspector has filed the HC-NIC Page 10 of 12 Created On Mon Aug 21 11:32:22 IST 2017 R/CR.MA/4599/2009 JUDGMENT complaint after the expiry of self life of the sample in question,
the respondents accused have lost their valuable right of sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory and therefore, the complainant Food Inspector has violated the mandatory provision of the Act.
Hence, the Trial Court has not committed any error while discharging the respondents accused and therefore, no interference is required in this Revision Application."

11. Keeping in view the aforesaid decisions rendered by this Court as well as the Hon'ble Supreme Court and the factual aspects discussed hereinabove, it can be said that in the present case, when the complainant-Food Inspector has filed the impugned complaint after expiry of shelf life of the sample in question, the applicant-accused has lost his valuable right of sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory and the complainant-Food Inspector has violated the mandatory provisions of the PFA Act.
Thus, only on this ground, the impugned complaint is required to be quashed and set aside.
12. Accordingly, this application is allowed.

The criminal complaint bearing no.27464 of 2008 for the offences punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 filed by respondent no.1 pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C.,Surat is hereby quashed and set aside qua applicant.
